item.title: Behind EU’s December asylum relocation pledges: More deal-making, fewer transfers
item.description: Most commitments made by EU states in December to receive asylum seekers arriving primarily in Italy and Greece are actually alternative forms of support.

item.title: Five ways the EU has already appeased Trump
item.description: Donald Trump has been back in White House for just over a year, and EU has struggled to balance safeguarding its own economic and social interests while maintaining a US relationship it needs to its security. Here are five ways the EU is adjusting to — many would say appeasing — Trump’s agenda.

item.title: THIS WEEK: Russian sanctions, Ukrainian loan and US trade deal
item.description: This week, the EU advances its agenda with new Russia sanctions, a potential deal on the €90bn Ukraine aid package, the EU's budget amendments, and talks on the US-EU trade deal.

item.title: Listen: Can Brussels ensure safe abortion for women everywhere in the EU?
item.description: Abortion bans pushed Polish women to seek risky or costly alternatives. Now the EU faces a showdown: can a new solidarity fund guarantee safe access across borders, or will politics block women’s rights again?

item.title: Two very different demonstrations in Paris — and what they tell us about the Iranian opposition and EU politicians
item.description: Any approach to current events in Iran that is driven primarily by self-interest and opportunism – condemning human rights abuses perpetrated by the regime, while readily ignoring violations by other actors – risks alienating the Iranian population in the long term, regardless of whether the Islamic Republic endures or not.

item.title: EU has ‘no concrete conclusions’ on Mandelson’s Epstein emails as trade commissioner
item.description: Peter Mandelson wrote numerous emails to child sex offender Jeffrey Epstein during his time as EU trade commissioner, 2004 to 2008.

item.title: Israel lets trickle of injured Gazans leave, while EU sanctions ‘on the shelf’
item.description: Israel opened the Rafah crossing point from Gaza to Egypt for six hours per day from Monday, allowing out 50 patients a day, accompanied by two relatives each in what it called a "pilot scheme".

item.title: Protests against Cargill in Brazilian Amazon are sign of EU-Mercosur blind spot
item.description: In Brazil’s Tapajós region, hundreds of Indigenous people have been protesting for days outside a Cargill export facility, opposing a federal decree that opens Amazonian rivers to private concessions and expanded dredging.

item.title: Bloc needs to ‘up its game’ on securing raw materials, auditors find
item.description: The three areas of improvement needed, according to the Luxembourg-based European Court of Auditors (ECA), are diversification of trade partners, more domestic production, and recycling, reusing and substituting.
